Grip giving out before your back does is common, and it's a training problem we can fix. Three things help:

- Hang from the bar for time at the end of your pull-up sessions. Work up to 30 to 45 seconds per hang, a few sets, and add time before you add anything else.
- Use a full grip with your thumb wrapped around the bar, and squeeze the bar hard as you pull instead of just hanging on. It also recruits more of your lats.
- Carry something heavy. Farmer carries with dumbbells or a trap bar build grip fast, and they fit on a pull day or a leg day.

Chalk helps if your gym allows it. I'd avoid straps for now, since they only hide the weak link while you're building it.

If you tell me where you train, I can build the hangs and carries into your program.
